news.title: Here we come! Young Ferns qualify for 2027 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: New Zealand have qualified for next year’s FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco after beating Papua New Guinea 3-0 in Honiara. The win, in the semi-finals of the OFC U-16 Women’s Championship, ensures New Zealand will be one of Oceania’s two representatives at the 2027 global tournament. It will be New Zealand’s 11th consecutive appearance at the U-16 World Cup. The second qualifying spot at the World Cup will go to either New Caledonia or Fiji, due to meet in Wednesday’s second semi-final.

news.title: Thomas Tuchel makes bizarre admission about eating World Cup grass
news.lede: Thomas Tuchel looks back on Mexico City celebrations with some regret (Picture: PA Wire) England manager Thomas Tuchel has a strange regret about the World Cup over the summer, wishing he had eaten some Mexican grass when he got the chance. The Three Lions had an eventful journey at the World Cup, reaching the semi-finals where they suffered a dramatic late defeat to Argentina. There were plenty of highs along the way, including the opening win over Croatia and finishing their tournament with a thrilling third-place play-off victory over France. The highlight for many, though, was the trip to the Azteca Stadium in the round of 16 and the tense 3-2 win England managed to secure over Mexico.

news.title: Spain: De la Fuente extends contract until 2030 after World Cup triumph
news.lede: The World Cup-winning coach has reached an agreement to remain in charge of La Roja for an additional two years, until the 2030 World Cup co-hosted by Spain. Luis de la Fuente has reached an agreement to extend his contract with the Spanish national team until the 2030 World Cup. The 65-year-old coach, who was previously contracted until Euro 2028, will now remain at the helm of La Roja as they defend their world title. The two-year extension was revealed on Tuesday, September 15, by public radio RNE and reported by Reuters.

news.title: Thomas Tuchel names one World Cup 'regret' as England boss reflects on 'painful' failure
news.lede: Thomas Tuchel has bizarrely revealed he regrets not eating the GRASS from England’s iconic World Cup win against Mexico . The Three Lions took on the joint-host nation in the last-16 of the competition in the summer. And they secured one of their most memorable results, securing a thrilling 3-2 victory. Jude Bellingham scored twice in two minutes, with Julian Quinones hauling the Central American side back into the game.

news.title: Roman Vega: The surprise inclusion in Argentina’s post-World Cup squad
news.lede: The defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final marked the end of one chapter for Argentina. But as Lionel Scaloni announced his squad for the national team's first three friendlies since that painful night, it became clear that the next chapter would look different. There was continuity, certainly. But there were also absences, suspensions, returning faces and, most intriguingly, a collection of young players knocking loudly on the door.

news.title: Messi set for Argentina farewell in Benin friendly | Gulf Times
news.lede: Lionel Messi was on Tuesday named in Argentina's squad for a friendly against Benin on October 6, a match that will serve as his farewell appearance after announcing his international retirement last month. The 39-year-old said in August he was retiring from Argentina duty after a two-decade international career that included winning the 2022 World Cup and Copa America triumphs in 2021 and 2024." We made the decision to invite the best player in the world, the symbol of our national team, our captain, Lionel Andres Messi, so that he can have the farewell he truly deserves on October 6 here in Argentina," said Argentine FA president Claudio Tapia.

news.title: Casablanca will host 2030 World Cup final, says Moroccan federation chief
news.lede: The 2030 World Cup final will be held in Casablanca, the President of the Royal Moroccan Football Federation was reported as saying by Spanish news agency EFE on Thursday. Soccer's world governing body FIFA has yet to announce the venue of the final, with Spain and Morocco in a heated battle to host soccer's biggest showpiece match. "The province of Benslimane will have the honour of hosting the 2030 World Cup final," Fouzi Lekjaa told a political party event in Bouznika, Morocco on Thursday, EFE reported. Benslimane is a city 60km from Casablanca and the site of the $12-billion Hassan II stadium, which is being built for the World Cup with a projected capacity of 115,000.
